letterTips.Aa: Like English 'a' but clearer and longer. Don't drop the final sound.
letterTips.Bb: Like English 'b', but press the lips together more firmly.
letterTips.Cc: Before e/i/y it sounds like 'ts'; before a/o/u like 'k'.
letterTips.Dd: Like English 'd' but unaspirated. At word end it sounds like 't'.
letterTips.Ee: Keep the mouth slightly open and hold the sound. Don't glide.
letterTips.Ff: Like English 'f'. The lower lip touches the upper teeth.
letterTips.Gg: Like 'g' in 'go', not 'j'. At word end it sounds like 'k'.
letterTips.Hh: A soft exhale, like English 'h'. No throat vibration.
letterTips.Ii: Short and clear, like a brief 'ee'. Don't lengthen it.
letterTips.Kk: Like English 'k' but more strongly aspirated.
letterTips.Ll: Put the tongue tip behind the upper teeth. Clearer than English 'l'.
letterTips.Nn: Like English 'n'. Tongue tip touches the upper gum.
letterTips.Oo: Round the lips and hold the position. Don't glide.
letterTips.Pp: Like English 'p' but more strongly aspirated.
letterTips.Qq: Always paired with 'u', pronounced 'kv'. E.g. Quelle = kvelle.
letterTips.Rr: A soft guttural roll at the back of the throat.
letterTips.Ss: Before a vowel at word start it sounds like 'z'; at word end like 's'.
letterTips.Tt: Like English 't', aspirated. Unchanged at word end.
letterTips.Uu: Firmly round the lips and keep it short.
letterTips.Ww: Pronounced like English 'v'. E.g. Wasser = Vasser.
letterTips.Yy: Like a short 'ü', or 'i' in Greek/English loanwords.
letterTips.Ää: Open the mouth wider than 'a', close to 'e' in 'bed'.
letterTips.Öö: Round the lips like 'o' but try to say 'e'. Tongue forward.
letterTips.Üü: Round the lips like 'u' but try to say 'ee'. Practice a lot.
letterTips.ß: German only, pronounced like 'ss'. After a long or double vowel.

cheatsheetPage.title: Grammar Cheatsheet
cheatsheetPage.subtitle: A quick summary of key grammar rules
cheatsheetPage.tipArticleDefinite: Tip: Only the masculine accusative changes (der → den). Dative always has -m (dem) except feminine -r (der) and plural -n (den).
cheatsheetPage.tipArticleIndefinite: Note: Indefinite articles have no plural form. Use "keine" for plural negation.

community.rulesSubtitle: Apply to the Vocabulary Arena and Speaking Rooms. By joining you agree to the rules below.
community.rulesBetaBody: The Arena and Speaking Rooms are new — we're listening to feedback to refine both features and rules. If something seems off or missing, please send feedback via the "🐞 Report · Feedback" button in each feature.
community.rule1Body: Don't insult, belittle, or mock other players in room names, messages, or voice. Everyone here is learning — treat others as you'd want to be treated.
community.rule2Body: Answer with your own knowledge. No auto-answer bots, pre-opened dictionaries, or asking others for answers. We can detect abnormal response times and flag accounts.
community.rule3Body: Don't mass-create rooms to spam the list, don't send repeated answers, don't harass via invite codes or passwords. Each round has a 50-attempt limit to prevent brute-force.
community.rule4Body: Speak German/Vietnamese in a friendly way. No profanity, no 18+ content, no advertising external services. Your mic streams live to your partner — behave as if meeting in person.
community.rule5Body: Use meaningful room names (e.g. "A2 review room", "Tan & friends"). Avoid profanity, political incitement, or ads. Room passwords are short strings to share with friends — not sensitive data.
community.rule6Body: Press the "🐞 Report · Feedback" button in each beta feature to report rule-breaking players. Brief description + time it happened. We review within 48 hours.
community.rule7Body: 1st time: warning. 2nd time: 7-day suspension from Arena / Speaking Rooms. 3rd time: permanent account ban. Severe behaviour (threats, sexual harassment, leaking others' personal info) may be banned immediately without warning.
community.rule8Body: Don't share email, phone, or address of yourself or others via rooms. Display name, avatar, and CEFR level are all opponents need to see.

topicDetail.tipsA1_1: All German nouns are capitalised and have a gender: der (masc.), die (fem.), das (neut.). Learn the gender with the word!
topicDetail.tipsA1_2: Basic sentence structure: Subjekt + Verb + Objekt. Example: Ich trinke Wasser.
topicDetail.tipsA1_3: Plurals usually change: -e, -en, -er, -s or Umlaut (ä/ö/ü). Example: das Haus → die Häuser.
topicDetail.tipsA2_1: Compound nouns (Komposita) are very common: Kühl + Schrank = Kühlschrank. The gender follows the last word.
topicDetail.tipsA2_2: Time adverbs: gestern (yesterday), heute (today), morgen (tomorrow) go at the start or after the verb.
topicDetail.tipsA2_3: Note Dativ after these prepositions: mit, nach, bei, seit, von, zu, aus → always take Dativ.
topicDetail.tipsB1_1: Verb prefixes change meaning: ver- (transform), be- (act on), ent- (separate), er- (achieve).
topicDetail.tipsB1_2: Nebensätze (subordinate clauses): the verb always goes to the end. Example: Ich weiß, dass er krank ist.
topicDetail.tipsB1_3: Learn Redewendungen (idioms) to sound more natural: "Hals- und Beinbruch!" = Good luck!
topicDetail.tipsB2_1: Genitiv grows more important: während des Sommers, trotz des Regens, wegen des Wetters.
topicDetail.tipsB2_2: Read German news (Spiegel, Zeit) to expand specialised vocabulary.
topicDetail.tipsB2_3: Konjunktiv II for politeness: Könnten Sie mir bitte helfen? instead of Können Sie mir helfen?
